title: Stage wrap-up: the complete prompt
summary: Put every technique together for a real task for your shop

steps.body:
Congratulations — you've almost finished Stage 1! 🎉 Let's review with a **good prompt checklist**:

1. **Context**: who you are, what's going on, what result you want
2. **Role**: who the AI should act as, like a marketer or a teacher
3. **Example**: show the AI something you like
4. **Format**: a list? How many points? How long?
5. **Tone**: polite, friendly, playful
6. **Limits**: what to avoid, budget, must-have conditions

Small tasks don't need all six, but **the bigger and more important the task, the more you include, the better**.

steps.bad: Make a marketing plan for my shop
steps.prompt:
You're a marketer who helps small shops with Facebook.
I run a homemade bakery in Chiang Mai. Most customers are office workers and students nearby. Next week I want people to discover our new pandan cake.
Plan 7 days of posts, Monday to Sunday. For each day give: a theme, a one-line post idea and the best time to post.
Tone: friendly and warm, like this: “Fresh custard bread just out of the oven — the whole street smells amazing 🍞 Drop by!”
Limits: no ad budget; only one promotion: buy 3 get 1 free on Saturday and Sunday; don't say “best in Chiang Mai”.
steps.output:
Mon — Launch: “It's here! Our fragrant new pandan cake 🌿” (7:30)
Tue — Behind the scenes: a short clip of squeezing fresh pandan in the morning (12:00)
Wed — Chat: “Any pandan fans out there? Raise your hand 🙋” (12:00)
Thu — Customer love: a regular with their first slice (17:30)
Fri — Heads-up: “Buy 3 get 1 free starts tomorrow!” (17:30)
Sat — Deal day: a full display case, come on in (9:00)
Sun — Thank you: customer photos from the week, last day of the deal (9:00)
steps.note: This prompt uses all six: role (marketer), context (shop, customers, goal), format (7 days, 3 things per day), tone with an example, and limits (no budget, the deal, a banned phrase).

steps.question:
Which checklist item is this prompt still missing?
“You're a copywriter. I run a small nail salon in Chiang Mai and my customers are university students. Write 3 Facebook captions, max 2 lines each, in a cute, cheerful tone.”
options: Limits, like including the promo price or not overclaiming
steps.explain: It has a role (copywriter), context (nail salon, students), format (3 captions, max 2 lines) and tone — but no limits or must-have conditions.

steps.body:
Once you've sent a great prompt, remember what to do with the answer:
- **Follow up** and say exactly what to change
- **Break big tasks into steps** and go one at a time
- **Always check** key numbers and facts yourself
- **Save prompts that work as templates** for next time

Ready? Let's do a real task 💪

steps.task:
Your shop (or an imaginary one, like a som tam stall or an online clothing shop) needs a **one-week Facebook promotion plan**.

Write one prompt that uses as much of the checklist as you can: context, role, example, format, tone, limits.
rubric: Context: says what the shop is, where it is or who the customers are, and this week's goal
Role: tells the AI who to act as (e.g. marketer, Facebook expert)
Format: says how many days the plan covers and what each day should include
Tone or example: describes the tone wanted or gives a sample post they like
Limits: gives at least 1 condition (e.g. budget, current promotion, things not to say)
steps.placeholder: e.g. You're a marketer... I run a... Plan 7 days of posts...
